statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-84008 (GHSA-846f-f764-76mx) is a .NET denial of service issue in System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs: SignedCms.CheckSignature can repeatedly reparse attacker-controlled X.509 data, causing unauthenticated quadratic CPU exhaustion. Microsoft lists Windows, Linux and macOS as affected, with System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs 10.0.0 through 10.0.12 affected and 10.0.13 fixed, shipped with .NET 10.0.13 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-846f-f764-76mx, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/468, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.13/10.0.13.md). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 264 packages of the twelve published builds (10.0.2-r0, 10.0.3-r0, 10.0.4-r0, 10.0.5-r0, 10.0.6-r0, 10.0.7-r0, 10.0.8-r0, 10.0.9-r0, 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold. Implementation copies of System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs.dll are in the Microsoft.AspNetCore.App shared framework (aspnetcore10-runtime, and the .NET SDK and the ASP.NET Core runtime archive held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap), the SDK's own and F# directories and the ASP.NET Core runtime pack in dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap, and, in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts, the System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs nupkg, the ASP.NET Core and WindowsDesktop transport nupkg files and the ApiCompat.Task, Arcade SDK and Build.Tasks.Feed build-tool nupkg files, plus the VersionTools.Cli build-tool nupkg in 10.0.15-r0; several of these also hold a runtimes/win copy at the same version. Each copy carries the build's own .NET version, except the build-tool copies, which can lag: the aarch64 10.0.13-r0 build holds 10.0.10 copies in the Arcade SDK and Build.Tasks.Feed nupkg files, and the 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0 builds hold 10.0.13 copies in the Arcade SDK, Build.Tasks.Feed and (in 10.0.15-r0) VersionTools.Cli nupkg files. So 10.0.2-r0 to 10.0.10-r0 and the aarch64 10.0.13-r0 package hold unfixed copies, and from 10.0.14-r0 on every copy is 10.0.13 or later. The range ends at 10.0.14-r0 because it is the first published build with no unfixed copy on either architecture; the x86_64 10.0.13-r0 package already holds only fixed copies.

CVE-2026-84008 (GHSA-846f-f764-76mx, https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-846f-f764-76mx): SignedCms.CheckSignature can repeatedly reparse attacker-controlled X.509 data, causing unauthenticated quadratic CPU exhaustion. Affected: System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs 10.0.0 to 10.0.12, fixed in 10.0.13; Microsoft shipped the fix in .NET 10.0.13 (SDK 10.0.113 and 10.0.402): https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/468, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.13/10.0.13.md. The dotnet10-sdk package ships its own copies of System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs.dll under /usr/lib/dotnet/sdk/<version>/ (the SDK root and FSharp directories, plus a Windows-specific runtimes/win copy), which the dotnet CLI, MSBuild, NuGet and F# tools load. Scanned every package built from the dotnet10-sdk source for Alpine 3.24 in the DHI Alpine repository (10.0.204-r0 to 10.0.303-r3, 8 builds; x86_64 and aarch64; including the -dbg, templates and doc subpackages, recursing into zip and NuGet archives) and read the version resources of every copy and the package versions recorded in the SDK's .deps.json files; both architectures match in every build. 10.0.204-r0, 10.0.301-r0, 10.0.302-r0, 10.0.302-r1 and 10.0.303-r0 carry System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs 10.0.8 to 10.0.12 (assembly product versions 10.0.8 to 10.0.12), inside the affected range; 10.0.303-r1 and every later build carry 10.0.13 to 10.0.15 (the assemblies in 10.0.303-r1 report product version 10.0.13 although the SDK version is still 10.0.303), which include the fix; the 10.0.13 assembly is also larger than the 10.0.12 one.

Scanned every package built from the dotnet8-sdk source for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository (8.0.123-r0 to 8.0.134-r0, 9 builds, as 8.0.128, 8.0.130 and 8.0.132 were not published for 3.23; x86_64 and aarch64; including the -dbg, templates and doc subpackages, recursing into zip and NuGet archives) and read the version resources of every copy and the package versions recorded in the SDK's .deps.json files; both architectures match in every build. 8.0.123-r0 to 8.0.131-r0 carry System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs 8.0.1 (built from .NET runtime 8.0.23 to 8.0.31 sources), inside the affected range; 8.0.133-r0 and every later build carry System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs 8.0.2 (built from .NET runtime 8.0.33 and later sources), which includes the fix; the fixed assembly is also larger than the previous one. The Roslyn build-task .deps.json still records an older 6.0 reference to the package, but no 6.0 copy of the assembly ships in any build.

CVE-2026-84008 (GHSA-846f-f764-76mx): SignedCms.CheckSignature in System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs can repeatedly reparse attacker-controlled X.509 data, causing quadratic CPU use. Microsoft fixed it in System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs 10.0.13, shipped with .NET 10.0.13; versions 10.0.0 to 10.0.12 are affected (https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-846f-f764-76mx, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/468). DHI dotnet-sdk-10 for Debian 13 repackages Microsoft's .NET SDK. Unpacked every published dotnet-sdk-10 package in the DHI Debian repository, 10 builds from 10.0.301-0 to the current 10.0.404-1 for amd64 and arm64, including the .nupkg archives inside them, and read the file and product version of every copy of System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs.dll; both architectures agree in every build. Each build carries copies in the ASP.NET Core shared framework (shared/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App) and in the SDK directory and its FSharp directory, each also under runtimes/win/lib/net10.0 in the SDK and FSharp directories, and in each build every copy has the same version: 10.0.9 in 10.0.301-0, 10.0.10 in 10.0.302-0 and 10.0.302-1, 10.0.11 in 10.0.400-1, 10.0.12 in 10.0.401-0 and 10.0.401-1, 10.0.13 in 10.0.402-0, 10.0.14 in 10.0.403-0, and 10.0.15 in 10.0.404-0 and 10.0.404-1. No .nupkg archive in these packages contains it. The dotnet-sdk-10-oci-config packages from the same source hold only a configuration file and a changelog. So 10.0.402-0 is the first build with the fixed assembly, and every earlier build carries an affected version. The range ends at 10.0.402-0.

CVE-2026-84008 (GHSA-846f-f764-76mx): SignedCms.CheckSignature in System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs can repeatedly reparse attacker-controlled X.509 data, causing unauthenticated quadratic CPU exhaustion. Microsoft lists System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs 8.0.0 to 8.0.1 as affected on .NET 8, fixed in 8.0.2, and shipped the fix in .NET 8.0.32 with SDK 8.0.426: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-846f-f764-76mx, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/468, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.32/8.0.32.md. DHI dotnet-sdk-8 for Debian 13 repackages Microsoft's .NET SDK. We read every published dotnet-sdk-8 build in the DHI Debian repository, 8.0.422-0 to 8.0.428-1 (10 builds, each for amd64 and arm64), after verifying each against its index checksum, recursing into the zip archives they carry, and read the version resources of every copy of System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs.dll and System.Security.Cryptography.Xml.dll; both architectures match in every build. No debug-symbol packages are published for this source, and the dotnet-sdk-8-oci-config package from the same source holds only a configuration file and its changelog. Every build carries System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs.dll in the ASP.NET Core shared framework under /usr/lib/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App/<version> and under /usr/lib/dotnet/sdk/<version> in the SDK root, FSharp, Containers/containerize, Containers/tasks and dotnet-watch tool directories, each of those SDK directories with a Windows-specific runtimes/win copy as well; 8.0.422-0 and 8.0.423-0 also carry two copies in the dotnet-format tool directory. In 8.0.422-0 to 8.0.425-1 every copy has file version 8.0.1024.46610 (product version 8.0.10), the assembly shipped in the System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs 8.0.1 NuGet package, except the dotnet-format copies in 8.0.422-0, which are version 8.0.0; both are in the affected range. From 8.0.426-0 on, every copy has file version 8.0.3226.50405 (product version 8.0.32), the assembly shipped in the fixed 8.0.2 NuGet package. The range ends at 8.0.426-0, the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-84008 (GHSA-846f-f764-76mx): SignedCms.CheckSignature in System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs can repeatedly reparse attacker-controlled X.509 data, causing unauthenticated quadratic CPU exhaustion. Microsoft lists System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs 8.0.0 to 8.0.1 as affected on .NET 8, fixed in 8.0.2, and shipped the fix in .NET 8.0.32 with SDK 8.0.426: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-846f-f764-76mx, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/468, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.32/8.0.32.md. DHI dotnet-sdk-8 for Debian 13 repackages Microsoft's .NET SDK. We read every published dotnet-sdk-8 build in the DHI Debian repository, 8.0.422-0 to 8.0.428-1 (10 builds, each for amd64 and arm64), after verifying each against its index checksum, recursing into the zip archives they carry, and read the version resources of every copy of System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs.dll and System.Security.Cryptography.Xml.dll; both architectures match in every build. No debug-symbol packages are published for this source, and the dotnet-sdk-8-oci-config package from the same source holds only a configuration file and its changelog. Every build carries System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs.dll in the ASP.NET Core shared framework under /usr/lib/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App/<version> and under /usr/lib/dotnet/sdk/<version> in the SDK root, FSharp, Containers/containerize, Containers/tasks and dotnet-watch tool directories, each of those SDK directories with a Windows-specific runtimes/win copy as well; 8.0.422-0 and 8.0.423-0 also carry two copies in the dotnet-format tool directory. In 8.0.422-0 to 8.0.425-1 every copy has file version 8.0.1024.46610 (product version 8.0.10), the assembly shipped in the System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs 8.0.1 NuGet package, except the dotnet-format copies in 8.0.422-0, which are version 8.0.0; both are in the affected range. From 8.0.426-0 on, every copy has file version 8.0.3226.50405 (product version 8.0.32), the assembly shipped in the fixed 8.0.2 NuGet package. The range ends at 8.0.426-0, the first published build with the fix.
